what: Clicking a same-site link sweeps an accent-color gradient tilted 20° (the first 20% is a soft edge) across the screen from bottom left to top right in .6s power2.out, then navigates after .5s. Once the new page has fully opened, the covering sheet lifts away in the same direction in .5s power2.out.

options.go: Time before moving on after press (s), default .5
options.out: Duration of clearing on a new page (s), default .5
options.cover: Cover the new page with a curtain when it opens (on/off), default on — set off where it opens without the reveal, like the first page
options.links: Whether to apply the cover (on/off), default on — the original first page goes without a curtain, so off
options.veil: Whether to draw the mask (on/off), default on — if off, there is no mask and it only moves on go seconds after the press

note: Links with #, new-window links and clicks already blocked by another handler are skipped. The curtain is position: fixed · z-index 70 · pointer-events: none. When returning from cache via back, a covering curtain is removed in .1s and lifted again. The original board skin writes the gradient stops as calc(0 + …%), so the whole background declaration is invalid — the curtain isn’t visible on screen and only a move delayed .5s after the click remains (the site copy is as measured with veil: off). The part’s default is the diagonal curtain the code intended

from.where: shared.js page transition — takes the intent of the original c-pageTransition (20deg gradient --progress .6s/.5s power2.out, navigates after 500ms) as the part default, while the site keeps the original screen as is: veil: off (only a .5s delay on sub-pages) · first page links: off
